title: Standardize synthetic corpus generation and seeding for regression runs
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: Our perf regression, eval pipeline, and load harnesses each implement their own synthetic sample/corpus generation and RNG seeding. This causes nondeterministic regressions, brittle CI flakes, and duplicated maintenance across adapters (loadgen, regression-runner, eval-orchestrator). Goal: create a single, lightweight seeding + synthetic-corpus library and migration plan so all harnesses produce reproducible, auditable inputs while preserving configurable randomness for stress scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: All perf-regression CI jobs use the new central seeding library (configurable via env var)
Regression runs reproducible: given a run_id and seed, re-running the job produces token-level identical prompts and deterministic latency profile within noise bounds
Load harness supports distributed seeding (shard-aware) with no collisions across runners
Documentation and a migration guide exist for in-repo adapters (loadgen, eval-scenarios, smoke controller)
At least three historical flaky regression scenarios are re-run and marked fixed or triaged with artifacts attached
tasks: Audit existing generators: list functions, seed sources, and format differences across harnesses
Design API for central library: deterministic seed derivation, shard-aware sequences, and optional entropy providers
Prototype library in python (lib/perf_seed) with minimal runtime deps
Add adapter wrappers for loadgen, regression-runner, and eval-orchestrator
Add unit tests and golden-corpus fixtures for seed determinism
Integrate new library into CI (workflow matrix job + reproducibility-check step)
Run migration on a canary repo, collect telemetry and failure modes
Rollout to production harnesses and update runbook + docs

notes: Trade-offs: keeping library minimal avoids adding heavy deps to runners, but requires small adapter shims in each harness. We intentionally avoid changing the canonical scenario formats in this work; format migration will be a follow-up. If HMAC-based run_id derivation is insufficient for some cross-team needs, we will expose a pluggable entropy provider.
follow_up: Post-rollout: schedule a 2-week observation window and capture SLO regressions
Follow-up ticket to migrate legacy scenarios to new canonical JSON shape
Add CLI tool to re-seed and replay historical runs from archived artifacts
